title: Borell scalar factor estimate
statement: Let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<q$, $q<p$, $p<1$, $0\leq\rho$, and $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$. For every natural number $m\geq2$, one has $\rho(m-q)\leq m-p$.
hypotheses_covered: Real numbers p, q, and rho
replaced: Let $0<q<p<1$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho^2=(1-p)/(1-q)$, and $m\in\mathbb N$ with $m\ge2$. Then $\rho(m-q)\le m-p$.
